title: Xiang and Xiao Rivers · Can a Map Feed You?
summary: The boatman's bargaining conceals the village's hardship. A mistaken channel is one wrong stroke on paper, but a season's meals in the fields.

S02-01.title: Xiang River Ferry
S02-01.summary: Youbai has barely praised the map's well-connected waterways when the boatman stops beside a dry channel. Would the spirit care to explain this connection?
S02-01.objective: Ask about the water and land routes to Riverbend Village
S02-01.result: You confirm that Riverbend Village can be reached by water or land, and hear of trouble with its water supply.
lines: All aboard for the crossing! Riverbend Village by water or land. Just don't follow a pretty map.
What do you mean, pretty? This map's waterways connect in every—
The boatman plants his pole beside the bank. Where the map shows a broad tributary, he raises a small puff of dust.
Direction? Hold that thought, elder. This one only carries a breeze.
The main river's roaring, but the fields' channel is dry. Copyists draw their blue lines. Crops can't drink ink.
Perhaps it is seasonal...
Then let's ask someone who lives here now. How do we reach Riverbend?
By boat to the village, or on foot along the old embankment. Terms first. Sailing second.

S02-02.title: Bargain with the Boatman
S02-02.summary: You prepare to haggle over the fare. The boatman turns his outstretched hand, revealing a palm caked with mud. His terms weigh more than a boat ride.
S02-02.objective: Use what you know of the routes and village to clarify the boatman's terms
S02-02.result: The boatman explains both routes. You may experience the water and land branches.
lines: Against the wind takes muscle. With the current takes care. Riverbend takes one more promise.
For the record, I'm not buying a boat or inheriting a family pier.
If you really mean to check that map, don't just glance at the village gate. Follow our channel problem through.
He opens his hand. Mud from last night's channel clearing remains packed between his fingers.
That outstretched hand wasn't asking for more money?
A poor fare means a few more crossings. Another season of dry fields means a boatload of people with no supper. Who pays that?
We'll look into it. Tell us what clues we can find on each route.
The old traveler knows the water route. The old embankment tells its own story on land. Either way, don't leave the village waiting for nothing.

S02-03.title: Share a Meal Aboard
S02-03.summary: You offer food. The old traveler uses two chopsticks to lay out the former channel on the deck. Apparently this boat carries an expert without a signboard.
S02-03.objective: Help the old traveler aboard and hear about the upstream water
S02-03.result: The traveler receives help. You learn that a branch channel is blocked, rather than the whole river running dry.
lines: Missed my meal while traveling. My stomach keeps better time than the oars.
I have some food. Eat first. No hurry to thank me.
Hot water too. He repaired these channels when he was young. Want to know the water? Ask him.
Only a few stretches. Lend me two chopsticks and I'll show you.
Holding his food down with one hand, the old man joins two chopsticks at an angle: the main river and the lower branch leading to the fields.
A hidden grandmaster of waterways aboard our boat.
Grandmasters need lunch too. The river hasn't stopped. The blockage is where these chopsticks meet.
Understood. This meal is on me. This lesson goes in my notes.

S02-04.title: Questions at the Village
S02-04.summary: The villagers dug a beautifully straight new ditch. The water insists on flowing back. Youbai checks the slope and decides to swallow its compliments.
S02-04.objective: Locate the water interruption using villagers' accounts and watermarks
S02-04.result: At the village's land entrance, you learn about the branch-channel inlet and the debris choking it.
lines: Dug it yesterday. Straight, isn't it? Nice and tidy?
Very straight. Why does it keep going uphill?
We were in a hurry. Followed the newly copied map. Here, let's pour in a bucket.
The water runs straight back down the ditch and around the villager's shoes.
A channel with lofty ambitions. Unfortunately, the water has not mastered lightness skills.
Stop digging for now. Where was the old inlet? Did it carry water before?
At the bend in the old embankment. It only stopped after bamboo and rubbish washed down a few days ago.
Then we'll check the old inlet. One wrong line on a map can mean days of extra digging.

S02-05.title: Restore Riverbend's Water
S02-05.summary: The sound of water leads to the old inlet, plugged tight with bamboo. Pulling out that stopper will do more good than ten handsome new ditches.
S02-05.objective: Enter task map 1-3, investigate the watercourse, and clear the correct inlet
S02-05.result: The branch inlet is cleared, restoring water to the fields. The village elder arrives to inspect it, and the irrigation task is complete.
lines: Everyone's here! Tell us where to dig and we'll dig!
Set the hoes down first. Less digging might help today.
Bamboo, leaves, and silt choke the low old inlet. Beyond it, the main river still flows. The new high ditch stretches uphill.
Like a teapot with a blocked spout, while everyone busily installs windows in the lid.
Then I was yesterday's hardest-working window fitter.
No need to blame anyone. Find where the river meets the field channel. Then we'll work together.
I'll watch downstream. When it's clear, release a little water first. Don't wash away the banks.
Good. Let's give the water its road back.
hints: Find the break between the flowing main river and the dry field channel.
Bamboo and silt block the old inlet. That channel slopes down to the fields; the new ditch climbs uphill.
Choose to remove bamboo and leaves from the old branch inlet and clear its silt.
options: Remove bamboo, leaves, and silt from the old inlet
The water finally finds its proper commute and runs through the old channel into the fields.
Extend the new high ditch farther uphill
An ambitious ditch, but the water won't cooperate. Check the inlet and slope.
Block the main river and wait for it to turn
The elder waves you off: Fixing one small channel doesn't require a large new problem for the whole village.

S02-06.title: The Old Xiao River Map
S02-06.summary: The elder produces no grand village treasure. He unfastens his cuff. The useful old map has long been softened by sweat and field mud.
S02-06.objective: Correct the old Xiao River map using the actual waterways
S02-06.result: You verify and annotate the old Xiao River map, gaining a lead to Liuzi Temple in Yongzhou.
lines: Looking for the old map? Right here.
The elder unfastens his cuff and takes out a soft oilcloth bundle. Its water lines are plain, its creases thoroughly earned.
You carry it against your skin? No ceremonial case?
I need it in the fields. Put it on an altar and who'll find the channels? Those gilded copies keep getting farther from home.
Bend Channel, Field Ditch... The same water has different names upstream and down. Someone copied it as two waterways.
Exactly. The water runs through today. Time that line did too.
I'll join the inlet and both local names in one note. Could you also check the old road to Yongzhou?
Follow downstream to Liuzi Temple. The old records and inscriptions are still there. Ask again when you reach anything uncertain.

S02-07.title: Thanks by the Basket
S02-07.summary: The villagers' gifts circle back to those who cleared the channel. Youbai stretches up for praise and receives a generous whiff of spring onion.
S02-07.objective: Accept the villagers' thanks and acknowledge everyone's irrigation work
S02-07.result: You exchange thanks with the villagers and record their shared work clearing the channel.
lines: Homegrown vegetables! Not worth much, but they'll make a hot meal on the road.
One handful reaches your arms as another basket arrives from the other side. You hurriedly share the first bunch with the workers.
Easy! This is a travel pack, not a mobile vegetable market.
I supervised throughout. Surely I am entitled to—
Would the elder like a sniff of fresh spring onions?
...A fragrant and substantial tribute.
Everyone restored this water. The notes can't make it all about us.
Write down whoever you like. But take some vegetables. You can't put credit on paper in a cooking pot.

S02-08.title: The Map and Its Makers
S02-08.summary: You ask who drew the old map. The elder counts on his fingers for a while. Some could write and some couldn't, but the roads they walked are all there.
S02-08.objective: Hear how the old map was kept and passed down
S02-08.result: You add the map's origins and its makers' spoken accounts to your evidence record.
lines: Elder, who drew this map? I'd like to record where it came from.
Grandfather made the first stroke. Later the boatmen added water levels, farmers moved the inlets, and those who could write recorded things for those who couldn't.
Wouldn't the credits be longer than the map?
If they won't fit, don't just write one grand name. No single person dug the channel.
He holds a corner flat. The mud beneath his nails looks much like the pale brown handprints on the old paper.
I understand. Record how it traveled, and who actually witnessed each claim.
If it's wrong, come back and ask. Don't turn us into old immortals nobody is allowed to correct.
That... I shall remember.
